code_actions.rationale: Treating team documents an 'open-book' (Tile B1) pelvic ring injury and explicitly documents the pelvis as 'unstable to lateral compression' with external fixation; policy requires surgeon-determined stability and unstable ring maps to S32.811A (MCC).

No documentation of cardiogenic pump failure; shock is repeatedly attributed to traumatic/hemorrhagic causes with MTP activation and operative hemorrhage control, so R57.01 (cardiogenic shock) is unsupported.
Admitting H&P lists AKI (KDIGO 2) associated with rhabdomyolysis (present on admission) and discharge documents resolved AKI; therefore POA should be Y and N17.9 is supported as CC.
Discharge documentation describes hospital-acquired MSSA ventilator-associated pneumonia treated during the stay; policy requires J95.851 be POA=N and is MCC.

No documentation of active or historical nicotine dependence was found in the reliable parts of the chart; admitting H&P states non-smoker and no other note supports nicotine-dependence; remove Z87.891.

No explicit operative/procedural documentation retrieved supports insertion of an external fixation device into the right upper femur specifically; the record documents pelvic external fixation and subsequent intramedullary nailing of the femur. Remove 0QH60BZ unless the definitive OR/IR procedure note shows it was performed.

Insertion of an infusion device into the SVC (port/central infusion device) was not explicitly documented in the retrieved operative/procedure summaries; remove unless supporting procedure/operative documentation is provided.

The claim printed description and the critical-care notes indicate MSSA as cause of VAP and cefazolin treatment; the billed organism code's printed description on the claim was wrong per CONFLICT (code vs description). Recode to the correct MSSA cause-code that matches documentation. Human coder confirmation requested to ensure the correct B95.* code is applied.

The discharge summary documents rhabdomyolysis with AKI; the billed M62.88 was flagged as not valid on the discharge-date code set. Record supports a rhabdomyolysis diagnosis and should be mapped to the correct, valid ICD-10-CM rhabdomyolysis code. Human coder confirmation required for exact code (HITL).
H&P and CT explicitly document right-sided rib fractures (right ribs 4-8); policy differentiates laterality - change billed S22.42XA to the right-side code S22.41XA.

policy_citations.section: Validation Criteria › AAST Splenic Organ Injury Scale — Coding Reference
policy_citations.quote: AAST Grade: Grade IV; Injury Description: Segmental or hilar vessel laceration with >25% devascularization; ICD-10-CM Code: S36.032A; CC/MCC Status: MCC; Audit Action: Confirm grade; angioembolization or splenectomy expected

The distinction between stable (S32.810A — CC) and unstable (S32.811A — MCC) is made by the treating orthopedic or trauma surgeon based on CT findings and classification; auditors must not infer stability from radiographic report alone — explicit surgeon documentation of stability/instability is required.

policy_citations.section: Validation Criteria › Medical — Non-Operative Hemorrhagic Shock Resuscitation Pathway
policy_citations.quote: • Massive transfusion protocol (MTP) activation documented in nursing notes, blood bank records, or physician orders, with packed red blood cell units, FFP, and platelets administered in balanced ratio

system_note: Summary of what was billed: Principal diagnosis S36.032A (Major splenic laceration, MCC) with multiple additional trauma MCC/CC codes plus procedure set including splenectomy (07TP0ZZ), IR embolization (04L33DZ), chest tube (0WH30YZ), pelvic external fixation (0SH90BZ), femoral IM nailing (0QQ606Z), prolonged ventilation >96hrs (5A1D90Z), transfusion (30233N1), and others. What the record shows vs. policy: 1) Splenic injury: admitting H&P documents a Grade IV splenic laceration and describes emergent damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy and subsequent IR embolization, satisfying the Splenic Injury policy's Surgical/Splenectomy pathway for S36.032A (AAST Grade III-V → MCC) (evidence: H&P: CT panscan Grade IV; H&P: splenectomy; Discharge: post-splenectomy vaccinations) (Policy: S36.032A validation requires AAST grade or operative documentation) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.604; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.604; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b57-r3]. 2) Femoral shaft fracture: operative note / problem list and discharge state IM nailing for right femoral shaft fracture, satisfying S72.301A surgical IMN pathway (MCC) and matching the billed intramedullary fixation procedure (evidence: H&P problem list and Discharge Summary) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.249; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869]. 3) Pelvic ring fracture stability/tiering: the record explicitly documents an open-book (Tile B1) pelvic ring injury and that the pelvis was “unstable to lateral compression” with external fixation performed. Per the Pelvic Ring policy the auditor must use the treating surgeon's stability determination to choose S32.810A (stable, CC) vs S32.811A (unstable, MCC). The chart documents instability (Tile B1 / unstable), so the billed S32.810A (stable, CC) underreports severity — it should be S32.811A (unstable, MCC) (evidence: H&P problem list and exam; policy guidance on stability classification) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.249; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.604; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Pelvic-Ring-Disruption.docx-b14]. 4) Shock codes: the clinical documentation repeatedly attributes the hemodynamic collapse to traumatic/hemorrhagic shock with MTP activation and urgent hemorrhage control (splenectomy and IR embolization). There is no documentation of cardiogenic pump failure; therefore the billed cardiogenic shock code R57.01 is unsupported and should be removed. T79.4XXA (traumatic shock) is supported by the record and policy (evidence: H&P describing hypotension SBP 78, MTP activation, operative hemorrhage control; Discharge summary states 'hemorrhagic shock') [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.604; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Traumatic-Shock.docx-b36]. 5) Acute kidney injury (N17.9): the admitting H&P documents rhabdomyolysis with AKI (KDIGO 2) and explicitly states non–dialysis-requiring AKI on admission; this supports N17.9 as present-on-admission (POA=Y, CC) rather than POA=N as billed (evidence: H&P problem list and Discharge Summary) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.249; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869]. 6) Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851): the Discharge Summary documents hospital-acquired MSSA VAP treated with cefazolin and the policy requires J95.851 to be assigned POA=N and carries MCC severity; the claim currently lists J95.851 but the billed tier/POA needs correction to reflect MCC/POA=N per policy (evidence: Discharge Summary and VAP policy) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869; RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b73]. 7) Organism code B95.62: the discharge documentation identifies MSSA as the causative organism of the VAP, but the billed organism code was recoded to B95.61 to match the documented MSSA cause-code and the claim print/description conflict; recode to B95.61 is supported by the record. Human coder confirmation requested to ensure correct B95.* code application. 8) Rhabdomyolysis code: the discharge summary documents rhabdomyolysis with AKI; the billed M62.88 was invalid on the discharge-date code set and the record supports mapping to the correct, valid ICD-10-CM rhabdomyolysis code M62.82. Recode to M62.82 and request human-coder confirmation. 9) Rib laterality: H&P and CT explicitly document right-sided rib fractures (right ribs 4-8); change billed S22.42XA to the right-side code S22.41XA. 10) Procedures: operative and procedure-level documentation in the H&P and Discharge Summary support splenectomy (07TP0ZZ), IR embolization (04L33DZ), chest tube / tube thoracostomy (0WH30YZ), pelvic external fixator (0SH90BZ), intramedullary nailing of the right femur (0QQ606Z), transfusion (30233N1), endotracheal intubation (0BH17EZ), and ventilator assistance >96 hrs (5A1D90Z). Two billed procedure items lack explicit supporting text in the retrieved extracts: insertion of an external fixation device into the right upper femur (0QH60BZ) and insertion of an infusion device into the superior vena cava (02HV33Z). The record documents pelvic external fixation and IM nailing of the femur but does not show documentation of a right femoral external-fixation placement nor a SVC infusion-device insertion in the retrieved notes; these two lines will be removed unless the definitive operative/procedural records show they were performed and are confirmed (evidence: Discharge Summary, H&P, Transfer Instructions) [NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.249; NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1091 p.867]. Conclusion and audit action: Finding. Changes required: remove unsupported cardiogenic shock (R57.01) and remove personal history of nicotine dependence (Z87.891) (no documentation of nicotine dependence; H&P notes non-smoker), recode pelvic ring injury from S32.810A (stable, CC) to S32.811A (unstable, MCC) based on surgeon-documented instability, correct N17.9 POA to Y (present on admission), change J95.851 severity/POA to MCC / POA=N in the claim record per policy, remove procedures 0QH60BZ and 02HV33Z if no operative note confirms those insertions, recode B95.62 → B95.61 to match documentation of MSSA, recode M62.88 → M62.82 for rhabdomyolysis, and recode S22.42XA → S22.41XA for laterality. All kept diagnoses/procedures are listed in code_decisions below with citations. Key citations (document / page): H&P (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9 p.604/p.249) documents Grade IV spleen, pelvic instability (Tile B1), right femur fracture and IM nailing, rhabdomyolysis with AKI; Discharge Summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095 p.869) documents IR embolization, pelvic external fixation, right femoral IM nailing, MSSA VAP treated with cefazolin, resolved rhabdo/AKI, and extubation on ICU day 9 (>96 hrs). Policy citations: Splenic Injury (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Splenic-Injury.docx-b57-r3), Pelvic Ring (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Pelvic-Ring-Disruption.docx-b14), Traumatic Shock (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Traumatic-Shock.docx-b36), VAP (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-Ventilator-Associated-Pneumonia.docx-b73).
rationale_letter:
Re: DRG audit of MR_12 — Determination and required coding corrections We performed a DRG-level review of the inpatient stay for claim MR_12, comparing billed ICD-10-CM/ICD-10-PCS codes and POA/CC-MCC flags to the treating-provider documentation and our governing coding policies. After reviewing the admission H&P, hospital course, and discharge/transfer summary and applying the cited DRG policy criteria, we found documentation-based discrepancies that affect CC/MCC assignment and one unsupported code. Summary of Findings and Audit Actions
1) Principal diagnosis (S36.032A - Major laceration of spleen, initial encounter) — Supported and remains principal. The admitting H&P documents a Grade IV splenic laceration and an emergent damage-control laparotomy with splenectomy; this meets the policy’s surgical pathway validation for S36.032A (AAST Grade III–V → MCC) (evidence: H&P CT panscan, operative description; Policy: Splenic Injury AAST table). 2) Pelvic ring injury — Recode required. The treating team documents an open-book (Tile B1) pelvic ring injury and explicitly documents the pelvis as “unstable to lateral compression” with external fixation performed. Per the Pelvic Ring policy the surgeon’s documented stability determination governs coding: an unstable pelvic ring (S32.811A) carries MCC status rather than the billed S32.810A (stable, CC). We will recode S32.810A → S32.811A (MCC). 3) Shock codes — Removal required. The clinical record attributes hypotension and shock to traumatic/hemorrhagic causes with Massive Transfusion Protocol activation and operative hemorrhage control (splenectomy and IR embolization). The record does not document cardiogenic pump failure to support R57.01 (cardiogenic shock). R57.01 is therefore unsupported and will be removed; T79.4XXA (traumatic/hemorrhagic shock) is documented and retained (MCC). 4) Acute kidney injury (N17.9) — POA correction. The admitting H&P documents rhabdomyolysis with AKI (KDIGO 2) that was present and managed on admission (non–dialysis-requiring). Therefore N17.9 should be POA=Y (present on admission), not POA=N as billed. 5) Ventilator-associated pneumonia (J95.851) — severity/POA correction. The discharge summary documents hospital-acquired MSSA ventilator-associated pneumonia treated with cefazolin; VAP is a hospital-acquired condition and the governing policy assigns MCC severity and requires POA=N. Update claim coding to reflect J95.851 as MCC with POA=N. 6) Organism (B95.62) — Recode required. The discharge summary documents MSSA as the causative agent of the VAP but the billed organism code and the claim description conflicted; the record supports recoding the billed B95.62 to B95.61 to match MSSA documentation. Human coder confirmation requested to ensure the correct B95.* code is applied. 7) Rhabdomyolysis (M62.88) — Recode required. The discharge summary documents rhabdomyolysis with AKI; the billed M62.88 was not valid on the discharge-date code set. Record supports rhabdomyolysis and should be mapped to the correct, valid ICD-10-CM rhabdomyolysis code M62.82. Human coder confirmation requested for final code selection. 8) Rib laterality (S22.42XA) — Recode required. H&P and CT explicitly document right-sided rib fractures (right ribs 4-8); change billed S22.42XA to the right-side code S22.41XA. 9) Procedures — Most billed procedures are supported (splenectomy, IR embolization, chest tube, pelvic external fixation, femoral IM nailing, transfusion, endotracheal intubation, and ventilation >96 hours). Two procedure lines lack explicit supporting text in the retrieved notes: insertion of external fixation device into the right upper femur (0QH60BZ) and insertion of infusion device into the superior vena cava (02HV33Z). Absent definitive operative/procedural documentation these lines should be removed; if supporting operative/procedure notes are provided showing these were performed, we will reconsider. Correction summary (claim-level): - Remove: R57.01 (cardiogenic shock); Z87.891 (personal history nicotine dependence) - Recode: S32.810A → S32.811A (unstable pelvic ring → MCC) - Recode: B95.62 → B95.61 (organism code to match MSSA documentation) - Recode: M62.88 → M62.82 (rhabdomyolysis) - Recode: S22.42XA → S22.41XA (rib laterality to right) - POA correction: N17.9 POA:N → POA:Y - Severity correction: J95.851 set to MCC (policy) and POA=N - Procedures: remove 0QH60BZ and 02HV33Z if no operative note confirms right femoral external-fixator insertion or infusion-device placement in the SVC; confirm with definitive operative/procedural records. Evidence relied on (select): H&P (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n9) documenting Grade IV splenic laceration, pelvic instability (Tile B1), right femur fracture and IM nailing, rhabdomyolysis with AKI; Discharge / Transfer Summary (NOTE-Medical-Records-1-15-MR_12.pdf-n1095) documenting IR embolization, pelvic external fixation, right femoral IM nailing, MSSA VAP treated with cefazolin, extubation on ICU day 9 (>96 hrs), and resolved rhabdomyolysis/AKI; Governing policy guidance for splenic injury, pelvic ring disruption, traumatic shock, and VAP (RULE-Policy-Documents-DRG-*). Next steps and appeal rights: The claim is adjusted per the corrections above. If the provider believes additional supporting documentation exists (operative notes, IR procedure notes, anesthesiology record, or radiology reports not included here) that would justify retaining any removed/replaced codes (particularly 0QH60BZ or 02HV33Z, or R57.01), please submit those definitive procedure/operative reports within 30 days for reconsideration. Sincerely, Medical Audit Team
